$comment: Operator levers over the fleet runner-selection watcher (scripts/runner_watch.py,
.github/workflows/runner-watch.yml). This repo runs the INSTANCE; the script was
authored in FuzeSDLC (PR #269) and the governance standards it implements
(required-checks.md 2.2.1, ci-runners.md) stay there. See the workflow header for why
the instance is here: the watcher is hosted-only by design, one of the two conditions
it detects is Actions-budget exhaustion, and in a PRIVATE repo a budget-exhausted
hosted job never starts - so it would have been dead exactly when it is needed.
The TARGET LIST is not here EITHER - it is FuzeSDLC's governance/ruleset-fleet.json,
the same one its ruleset_sync / repo_settings_sync / prune_merged_branches read, so a
repo joining the fleet joins the watcher with no second list to remember. It is NOT
vendored into this repo: runner-watch.yml fetches it with the fuze-agent App token and
passes --fleet-file, and FAILS if it cannot (an unknown fleet must never sweep clean).
This file - the levers - is genuinely local, because the levers are the instance's.
WHY `pinned` EXISTS. The closed PR #249 made vars.CI_RUNNER_LABELS the operator's
explicit override, evaluated FIRST in its precedence order. That arm could not survive
the shape change: in this design CI_RUNNER_LABELS is the watcher's OWN output, so
honouring it as an override would make the watcher permanently defer to its own last
write and never change anything again. The lever therefore moved HERE, to a separate
sink the watcher only ever reads. A repo listed in `pinned` is probed and REPORTED on
every run, and never written to — visibility is not what is being switched off.
`capability` marks repos whose jobs need in-cluster reach (kubectl / helm / argocd).
For those, a hosted runner is not a degraded option, it is a non-option
(governance/ci-runners.md §1), so the pin beats visibility AND beats liveness. It is
empty today: FuzeInfra is the fleet's one genuinely capability-split repo and it
is `excluded` from ruleset-fleet.json entirely - and is now also the HUB this
watcher runs from, so it is doubly out of its own reach: the watcher never writes
its own CI_RUNNER_LABELS. Left in place because the arm is real and the next repo
to grow a cluster job needs somewhere to say so.
`hysteresis` is the number of CONSECUTIVE runs that must compute the SAME new value
before it is written over the live one. DO NOT SET IT TO 1. This design persists its
decision, which is exactly what #249 avoided in order to make oscillation impossible;
the counter is what buys that guarantee back. At 1 a pool that flaps between two cron
ticks rewrites the runner of every repo in the fleet, and the next tick rewrites them
all back. scripts/__tests__/test_runner_watch.py asserts this file never ships below 2.
`stranded_minutes` is how long a job must sit `queued` with NO runner assigned before
the recovery job will cancel + re-dispatch its run. It is the one knob on a DESTRUCTIVE
operation, so it is deliberately generous: an ordinary busy-pool wait must never be
mistaken for a stranding. Lower it only with evidence about real queue times, not to
make a demo faster.
